docs.title: Cobblemon HMs
docs.text:
Your Pokémon lend you their moves. Send one out and it cuts trees, smashes rocks and lights caves with your bare fist, or gives you auras like Flash, Dive and Rock Climb while it stays near you.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Cobblemon 1.8+

Get started Every HM

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Send out a Pokémon and open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it.
  2. Pick Field moves: it lists every HM that Pokémon has in its movepool.
  3. Partner HMs go to your empty fist: one at a time, fired with a click.
  4. Auras run on you while the Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks.
  5. No hunger, nothing to learn and nothing to carry: just a cooldown per Pokémon.

4.0: the companion model

You no longer learn HMs. Every HM now comes from a Pokémon of yours that knows the move, the Trainer Ditto sells TMs, and the HM Case is a TM bag. What changed.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
The command root is /hms.

Who Commands 🙂 Every player list · mount 🛡️ Operators (level 2) list <player> · config … · trader …

There are no commands to learn, select or use an HM any more: your Pokémon lend them, from Cobblemon's interaction wheel (see Your Pokémon).

docs.title: Player commands
docs.text:
/hms list
Shows what your Pokémon are lending you right now: the HM on your fist and the auras in effect.

/hms mount
Reports what the mount boosts can see on the Pokémon you are riding. Useful for telling a broken boost apart from riding something you did not expect.

docs.title: Operator commands
docs.text:
Require permission level 2.

/hms list <player>
The same report, for another player.

/hms trader spawn [player]
/hms trader spawn shiny [player]
/hms trader forget [player]
Summons a Trainer Ditto on demand, or undoes a catch so it will visit that player again.

/hms config <ability> cooldown <0–24000>
/hms config <ability> power <0–512>
/hms config <ability> minlevel <0–100>
/hms config <ability> enabled <true|false>
/hms config <ability> reset
/hms config reset_all

/hms config activator button <left|right|either>
/hms config trader enabled <true|false>
/hms config trader every <ticks>
/hms config trader stay <ticks>
/hms config trader ivs <0–6>
/hms config trader levels <min> <max>
/hms config trader coins <min> <max>

After updating to 4.0

There is nothing to reset. Every save is migrated the first time each player joins — see Upgrading to 4.0. Retired HMs no longer answer any command.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Starts as the built-in defaults
  2. Saved in config/cobblemon_hms.json
  3. Changed with the Cloth Config screen (through Mod Menu) or /hms config
  4. Result the per-ability values the game uses

docs.title: Activation
docs.text:
A partner HM fires from your empty hand: there is nothing to hold and nothing to select. The one choice left is the button:

Setting Options Notes Activator button Left-click · Right-click · either (default) Left never opens chests or doors; right is answered by interactable blocks first 
/hms config activator button left|right|either

docs.title: Trainer Ditto
Per-ability values
docs.text:
Every HM has these tunable values:

Parameter Description Cooldown Ticks between uses (20 ticks = 1 second; 0 = no cooldown), counted per Pokémon Power Ability-specific: radius, duration, damage, count, level, etc. Required level Experience level needed before the HM will fire (every HM ships at 0) Enabled Off hides the HM from every Pokémon

Nothing costs hunger any more. The cooldown belongs to the Pokémon that lent the move, so a second Pokémon with the same move is ready straight away.

docs.title: Required level
docs.text: A requirement, not a price: nothing is deducted when the HM fires, you simply cannot reach for it until you have got there. Every HM ships at 0, so nothing is gated unless a pack says so. Switching an aura off is never gated, so raising a requirement can never strand someone inside an effect they cannot end.

docs.title: Cloth Config GUI (Fabric)
docs.text: Open Mod Menu → Cobblemon HMs → ⚙ to see sliders for every ability's values. Changes save automatically.

/hms config <ability> cooldown <0–24000>
/hms config <ability> power <0–512>
/hms config <ability> minlevel <0–100>
/hms config <ability> enabled <true|false>
/hms config <ability> reset

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
The file is saved at:

  • Fabric: config/cobblemon_hms.json
  • NeoForge: config/cobblemon_hms.json

You can edit it directly — changes take effect on next server start. Settings from before 4.0 that no longer do anything (hunger, trader weight, activator item) are left in the file and ignored.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Cobblemon HMs has nothing to learn, craft or carry. Your Pokémon do the work. If a Pokémon of yours has a move in its movepool, it can share it with you while it is out.

docs.title: Your Pokémon's wheel
docs.text:
Send out a Pokémon, open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it and pick Field moves. The wheel that opens lists everything that Pokémon can do for you, and nothing it cannot:

Kind What a pick does Page Partner HM That Pokémon lends the move to your empty fist Partner HMs Aura Switches a passive effect on you, on or off Auras Mount toggle Helps that Pokémon when you ride it Your Pokémon

A Pokémon can share a move when the move is in its movepool (equipped or not), or when its species is one listed on those pages. It has to be yours, sent out, and within 24 blocks.

docs.title: Using a partner HM
docs.text:
Once a Pokémon is lending you an HM, click with an empty hand to fire it. Anything else in your hand keeps its normal click, so tools, weapons and blocks behave exactly as they always did.

One Pokémon lends one HM at a time. Walk away from it and the HM pauses until you are back. Put it back in its ball and it stops lending, and its auras switch off too, weather included: send it out and switch them on again.

Getting your fist back

While an HM is lent, a bare-handed click fires it instead of punching. Open the Pokémon's wheel and pick the lent move again to hand it back, or simply recall the Pokémon.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: There is no hunger cost and nothing to pay. Each HM has a cooldown, kept per Pokémon, so a second Pokémon with the same move is ready straight away. Auras cost nothing at all.

docs.title: The Trainer Ditto
docs.text:
A rare wandering Trainer Ditto turns up now and then and sells three random Cobblemon TMs for relic coins. Right-click it to open its stall. Prices follow the power of the move, from 4 coins for a status move up to 32 for the strongest ones. Each TM is sold once per visit.

Keep what you buy in the HM Case, which holds any number of TMs.

It is a Ditto in a coat. Throw a Poké Ball and you catch it like any other, but every trader after that keeps its distance and will not open its stall for you again, so weigh the shop against the Ditto. How good that Ditto is is the server's call, and out of the box it rolls its IVs like any other: guaranteed perfect stats are an option an operator turns on, not something the trader comes with. See Configuration.

One in 8192 is shiny, at Cobblemon's own odds, and wears a shiny costume. Once caught it is an ordinary, non-shiny Ditto: the shine was the costume, not the prize.

Each trader wears a random player skin, and keeps it for as long as it stands there.

For resource pack makers: adding faces

Every PNG under assets/cobblemon_hms/textures/entity/trainer_ditto/ is in the pool, so a resource pack adds a face by dropping a file in. A file whose name contains shiny is kept for the shiny trader.

docs.title: Your Pokémon
docs.text:
Everything in Cobblemon HMs comes from your Pokémon. Send one out, open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it and pick Field moves. The second wheel lists everything that Pokémon can do for you:

  • Partner HMs it can lend your empty fist — see Partner HMs.
  • Auras it can give you while it is out and near you — see Auras.
  • Mount toggles that help it when you ride it — below.

A Pokémon can do any of these when the move is in its movepool (anything it can learn: by level, egg, tutor, TM, evolution or form change; it does not need to be one of its four moves), or when its species is one listed on these pages (the species that used to teach the HM).

No field moves any more

Celebrate is a partner HM now, and Rain Dance, Sunny Day and Blizzard are weather auras.

docs.title: Mount toggles
docs.text:
The toggles that make a ride better belong to the Pokémon you ride. Open the same Field moves wheel on it and switch them on there; a toggle that is on shows green. They stay on for that Pokémon — not for you, and not for your other mounts — and help it whenever it is ridden.

Disc Toggle Pokémon (any of) While it is on Surf Lapras, Kyogre, Suicune It cuts through water much faster. Tailwind Talonflame, Noivern, Staraptor It moves noticeably faster through the air. Swift Ninjask, Accelgor, Electrode It gets up to speed twice as quickly. U-turn Yanma, Ninjask, Venipede It turns far more sharply — on land, in water and in the air — up to the best handling a mount can have. Gliders, helicopters and burst swimmers have no handling stat, so it does nothing for them. Helping Hand Plusle, Minun, Audino It spends half the stamina on everything it does. Agility Alakazam, Jolteon, Aerodactyl It runs faster on land.

The Jump and Rock Climb auras also carry over to whatever you are riding.

docs.title: HM Case (TM bag)
docs.text:
Since 4.0 the HM Case is a bag for Cobblemon TMs. It holds as many as you like, of as many moves as you like, in one slot.

Right-click with the Case in hand to open it.

Do What happens Put TMs away Every TM in your inventory goes into the bag Click a row Takes one TM of that move out Shift-click a row Takes the whole stack out Type in the search box Filters the list by move name

The Case's tooltip shows how many TMs are inside. A TM taken out that does not fit in your inventory stays in the bag, so nothing is ever dropped.

The contents are stored on the Case itself, so it keeps them when you put it in a chest or hand it to a friend.

Where TMs come from

The Trainer Ditto sells three random TMs for relic coins every time it visits.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: The game will not start and names Cobblemon
docs.text: Cobblemon HMs needs Cobblemon 1.8.0 or newer. On 1.7.x it refuses to load with a dependency error rather than crashing mid-session. Update Cobblemon. The rest of what to install is in the table at the bottom of the home page.

docs.title: My punches fire an HM
docs.text: While a Pokémon is lending you an HM, a bare-handed click fires it instead of punching. Pick the lent move again in that Pokémon's wheel to hand it back, or recall the Pokémon. See Partner HMs.

docs.title: A Pokémon does not offer an HM
docs.text: It can only share a move that is in its movepool, or that its species is listed for. It also has to be yours, sent out, and within 24 blocks.

docs.title: An HM I had is gone after updating to 4.0
docs.text: In 4.0 you no longer learn HMs: your Pokémon lend them. Every trigger item you paid is handed back the first time you join, so there is nothing to reset. See Upgrading to 4.0.

docs.title: My old config file changed
docs.text: A config written before 4.0 is brought up to date on load, and only where the meaning of a value changed. Retired HMs drop out of the file. See Configuration.

docs.title: Upgrading to 4.0
docs.text: 4.0 renames the mod to Cobblemon HMs and turns it around: you no longer learn HMs, your Pokémon lend them to you. A Pokémon that has a move in its movepool can share it while it is out and near you. Everything that fights lives in Cobblemon Action Combat.

docs.title: The new name
docs.text:
Up to 3.x the mod was Ditto HMs. 4.0 renames everything, including the mod id (cobblemon_ditto_hms is now cobblemon_hms):

  • The jars are cobblemon-hms-fabric-… and cobblemon-hms-neoforge-…. Delete the old cobblemon-ditto-hms-… jar from mods/ when you update: the loader sees two different mods and would load both.
  • Your world carries over. HM Cases and discs in chests and inventories, everyone's HM save and the config file are read under the old name and saved under the new one.
  • The command is /hms (it was /dittohm).
  • The key binding for the HM wheel goes back to its default once.

docs.title: Your save
docs.text:
Nothing to do, and nothing you paid for is lost. The first time each player joins after the update:

  • Every HM you had learned is cleared, and its trigger item is handed back, or dropped at your feet if your inventory is full.
  • Old HM discs stay in chests as inert items, so you can still trade them away.
  • A chat message explains what happened.

The config file is updated too, and only where a value changed meaning; see Configuration.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• Nothing to learn. Open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on your Pokémon, pick Field moves, and it lists every HM that Pokémon can share. See Getting Started.
  • Partner HMs go to your empty fist, one at a time. See Partner HMs.
  • Auras run while the Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks. See Auras.
  • No hunger. The only cost is a cooldown, kept per Pokémon.
  • No HM wheel and no H key. Everything is in the Pokémon's own wheel.
  • The Trainer Ditto sells TMs for relic coins instead of teaching HMs.
  • The HM Case is a TM bag with a search box. See HM Case.

docs.title: What went where
docs.text:
HMs Partner HMs Cut · Rock Smash · Stockpile · Leafage · Strength · Teleport · Camouflage · Charge · Tail Whip · Growth · Minimize · Outrage · Calm Mind · Celebrate Auras Magnet Rise · Rock Climb · Dive · Jump · Flash · Lava Plume · Absorb · Lucky Chant · Shadow Sneak · Snowscape · Rain Dance · Sunny Day · Blizzard · Sweet Scent · new: Sandstorm · Fog Merged X-Scissor → Cut · Dig → Rock Smash · Rototiller → Leafage (crouch) · Water Gun and Eruption → Stockpile Your mount's toggles Surf · Tailwind · Swift · U-turn · Helping Hand · Agility Moved to Cobblemon Action Combat Bullet Seed · Explosion · Thunder · String Shot · Crabhammer · Mean Look · Harden · Burning Bulwark · Substitute · Destiny Bond · Egg Bomb · Protect · Whirlwind · Barrier · Acid Armor · Rock Throw · Boomerang · Powder Snow · Confusion Retired Fly · Glide · Headbutt · Thief · Present · Miracle Eye · Decorate · Rest · Defog · Revival Blessing · Charm · Bounce · Obstruct · Ember · Earthquake · Vine Whip · Waterfall

Fly is gone because travelling by air is what your flying Pokémon are for: ride one. Magnet Rise stays as a slow hover for building.

docs.title: Partner HMs
docs.text:
Partner HMs are the ones your empty fist fires. One of your sent-out Pokémon lends you one: open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it, pick Field moves, then "Lend me …". While that Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks, a click with an empty hand fires the HM. One Pokémon lends one HM at a time: picking another replaces it.

The only cost is a cooldown, kept per Pokémon: two Pokémon that both know Cut each have their own.

  1. Do Click with an empty hand
  2. Check A Pokémon of yours, out and near you, is lending the HM
  3. Check Your experience level is high enough (if the server sets one)
  4. Check That Pokémon's cooldown has run out
  5. Result The HM fires and that Pokémon's cooldown starts

If any check fails, nothing happens.

docs.title: Who can lend it
docs.text:
A Pokémon can lend an HM when the move is in its movepool (equipped or not) — including a move merged into it, so a Pokémon with Dig can lend Rock Smash — or when its species is one of these:

Disc HM Pokémon (any of) Camouflage Zorua, Kecleon, Ditto Charge Elekid, Electabuzz, Electivire Cut Scyther, Scizor, Kartana, Kleavor, Vikavolt Leafage Bulbasaur, Chikorita, Treecko, Snivy, Drilbur, Excadrill Rock Smash Hitmonchan, Machop, Geodude, Diglett, Dugtrio, Trapinch Stockpile Gulpin, Swalot, Squirtle, Totodile, Mudkip, Camerupt, Magcargo, Heatran Strength Machoke, Machamp, Conkeldurr Tail Whip Rattata, Sentret, Buneary Teleport Abra, Kadabra, Alakazam, Ralts Growth Sunkern, Sunflora, Petilil Minimize Ditto, Chansey, Barboach Outrage Dragonite, Salamence, Haxorus Calm Mind Alakazam, Espeon, Gardevoir Celebrate Jigglypuff, Ludicolo, Alcremie

docs.title: Camouflage
docs.text:
Cooldown: 15 min · Power: 18000t (15 minutes)

Become the living creature you're looking at. Your model is replaced by theirs — species, form, variant, gear and its nametag — for everyone who can see you.

  • Aim at a creature in clear view → you look exactly like it for 15 minutes.
  • Fire it again while you are wearing one → the costume comes off and the HM is ready immediately, so changing disguise is two presses.
  • A block, a wall between you and it, or empty air → nothing happens. You can only copy something you can actually see.
  • Other players can't be copied.

The disguise is a costume, not a creature: nothing extra exists in the world, so there is nothing to hit, nothing in your way, and nothing that can be killed off you.

docs.title: Charge
docs.text:
Cooldown: 3s · Power: ticks between sparks (10)

Turns the block you aim at into a redstone power source — enough to throw a door, a piston or a lamp from across a room. The charge is permanent. It is saved with the world, so it stays when you log off and when the server restarts, and charging another block does not take it back: charge as many as you like. Aim Charge at a charged block again to discharge it. Breaking the block ends its charge too.

The block is never replaced — it stays exactly what it is and simply answers as a power source — so you can charge a chest, a furnace, a statue or a wall without losing anything. While it is live it throws off electric sparks, so a charged block is one you can find again.

docs.title: Cut
docs.text:
Power: max 128 blocks

Aim at a log and the whole tree comes down — every connected log, with the leaves and vines tangled in it. Aim at a leaf or a vine and just that tangle goes.

It also cuts plants: grass, ferns, crops, ground cover. Those come away as if you had used shears, so the drops are the careful ones — the grass itself rather than a couple of seeds — and that holds for plants added by a datapack too, because it is the game's own loot tables answering.

With nothing to cut in front of you, it clears the ground around you (this is what X-Scissor used to do), in two passes of decreasing politeness:

  1. Weeds first — grass, ferns, dead bushes. If there are any, that is all it touches.
  2. Then what somebody planted — flowers and crops, and only once there is not a single weed left in range (radius 5). Casting by accident in your own wheat field costs you the weeds, not the field.

It never strips grass down to dirt: as a fallback, that would go off every time you missed a tree.

docs.title: Leafage
docs.text:
Cooldown: 2s · Power: radius 5

Instantly grows every crop around you to full maturity — handy for fast harvests — and does the same for saplings and berry trees.

The bare ground answers too, and it answers in flowers: a burst leaves a meadow rather than a lawn, with the odd blade of grass among it. The blooms are ones that belong to the biome you are standing in, so a burst in a plains looks nothing like one in a flower forest — and a biome with no flowers of its own gets grass rather than a dandelion that does not belong there.

It only ever plants on bare ground. A spot that already has something growing on it is left exactly as it stands, so casting twice in the same meadow thickens it instead of disturbing it, and tall flowers are planted whole rather than as a half that topples.

Only crops, saplings and berry trees are grown. Grass blades, ferns, moss, nylium, glow lichen and seagrass are left alone, so a burst never smothers the meadow it planted or creeps moss over the stone nearby.

Crouch while you use it to till instead (this is what Rototiller used to do): the dirt-type block you aim at, within your normal reach — Dirt, Grass Block, Coarse Dirt, Dirt Path — turns into Farmland. A flower or grass on it drops as an item. Tilling has no cooldown and does not use up the burst's.

It changes the world, so it needs the right to build: it does nothing in adventure or spectator mode, and skips spawn protection and claimed land. The radius (power) is capped at 16.

docs.title: Rock Smash
docs.text:
Power: max 32 ores

Instantly breaks the block you aim at. If it's an ore, vein-mines all connected ore of that type; otherwise breaks the single pickaxe-minable block (Netherite Pickaxe drops).

It digs too (this is what Dig used to do): dirt, sand, gravel and anything else a shovel takes come out in one hit, free, with a Netherite Shovel's drops.

docs.title: Stockpile
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1s · Power: lava self-damage 7 (3.5 hearts)

Stockpile is a mouthful you keep. It took over Water Gun and Eruption.

  • Aim at water or lava (source or flowing) and you drink it. The pool is drained, and that fluid is now what you carry. Water is free; lava is spicy and burns going down.
  • Aim anywhere else and you spit it back out on the face you are aiming at — the same square a bucket would fill. You can spit as often as you like: what you carry only changes when you drink the other fluid.
  • Spitting water at a sponge soaks it.

It passes the same permission check a bucket does, so claims, spawn protection and the world border all hold. Lava is never placed at your own feet, and water boils away in the Nether, as it would from a bucket.

docs.title: Strength
docs.text: Pushes the aimed block one block in whichever of the six directions you're looking — up and down included. Containers travel with their contents, and a double chest moves as one unit: both halves go together, or the push fails if either has nowhere to go. Won't move fluids.

docs.title: Tail Whip
docs.text:
Cooldown: 2s

Sweeps a suspicious sand or gravel block clean in a single motion instead of a dozen slow ones, and finds exactly what a brush would have found. Rooted dirt counts too: it is not brushable in vanilla, but it is the same gesture on the same kind of thing, so it gives up its hanging roots.

docs.title: Teleport
docs.text:
Cooldown: 30s · Power: max 30 blocks

Blinks you to the block you're looking at (≤ 30 blocks), finding the nearest safe landing. Plays the Enderman teleport sound.

It is the strongest way to travel the mod has, so it is priced like it: dearer than anything else you fire, and slow to come back.

docs.title: Growth
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1 min · Power: how long you stay big (5 minutes)

Aim at one of your Pokémon and it grows one size, for good. Aim at anything else, or at nothing, and it is you who grows, to twice your size, for a while.

docs.title: Minimize
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1 min · Power: how long you stay small (5 minutes)

Growth's opposite. Aim at a Pokémon and it shrinks one size, for good. Aim anywhere else and you go half-size for a while.

docs.title: Outrage
docs.text:
Cooldown: 5 min

Aim at an XL Pokémon to turn it into an Alpha. Anything smaller, it refuses.

docs.title: Calm Mind
docs.text:
Cooldown: 2 min

Aim at an Alpha to settle it back into the ordinary Pokémon it was. The way back out of Outrage.

docs.title: Celebrate
docs.text:
Cooldown: 10 min · Power: how many rockets (8)

Punch with an empty hand and a firework show goes up over your head, for no reason at all. The rockets are made for you, not taken from your inventory, and burst well above head height, so they hurt nobody.

docs.title: Auras
docs.text:
Auras are passive HMs your Pokémon give you while they are out and near you (24 blocks). Open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on one of your sent-out Pokémon, pick Field moves, and switch an aura on; it shows ✔ while it is on. Recall the Pokémon or walk away from it and the aura stops; it comes back when the Pokémon does.

You can run as many auras as you like, from one Pokémon or several. They cost nothing.

Put the Pokémon back in its ball and its auras switch off. Sending it out again does not bring them back: switch them on again from its wheel. Walking away from it only pauses them.

Weather auras

Rain Dance, Sunny Day, Blizzard, Sandstorm, Fog and Snowscape are weather. Only one runs at a time: switching one on, on any of your Pokémon, switches the others off, so the last one you switched on is the one in effect. Between players close together, too, the weather switched on last wins. Like any aura, a weather only works while its Pokémon is out and near you, and putting the Pokémon back in its ball switches it off.

Every weather takes over Minecraft's own sky while it is on: Rain Dance makes it rain, and all the others keep it clear, so no rain falls through your sandstorm, fog or blizzard while their own effects run. Switch it off, or recall the Pokémon, and the game decides the weather again.

What is on right now

Open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on any Pokémon: its top-left corner lists every HM in effect, each with the Pokémon doing it in brackets, by its nickname if it has one — for example Sandstorm (Dunes).

The toggles that make a mount better — Surf, Tailwind, Swift, U-turn, Helping Hand and Agility — belong to the Pokémon you ride: see Your Pokémon.

HUD icons

Every aura in effect shows its own HM status-effect icon in your HUD (top-right), so it's obvious at a glance which ones are on.

docs.title: Who can give it
docs.text:
A Pokémon can give an aura when the move is in its movepool (equipped or not), or when its species is one of these:

Disc Aura Pokémon (any of) Absorb Gulpin, Swalot, Victreebel Blizzard (weather) Abomasnow, Glalie, Froslass Dive Vaporeon, Lapras, Wailord Flash Ampharos, Jolteon, Lanturn Jump Magikarp, Buneary, Spoink Lava Plume Magcargo, Slugma, Turtonator Lucky Chant Clefairy, Chimecho, Togetic Magnet Rise Magnemite, Magneton, Magnezone Rain Dance (weather) Politoed, Kyogre, Golduck Rock Climb Rhydon, Rhyperior, Sneasel Shadow Sneak Gengar, Banette, Spiritomb Snowscape (weather) Froslass, Mamoswine Sunny Day (weather) Torkoal, Sunkern, Volcarona Sweet Scent Gloom, Bellossom, Vileplume, Aromatisse Sandstorm (weather) Hippopotas, Hippowdon, Tyranitar, Gigalith, Sandaconda Fog (weather) Gastly, Haunter, Koffing, Weezing, Misdreavus — or any Pokémon with Haze, Mist or Smokescreen

docs.title: Absorb
docs.text:
Power: magnet radius 6

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Loose items on the ground drift toward you while it is on, so a scattered drop or a mined vein gathers itself. Items are nudged rather than yanked, so they keep their normal pickup delay.

docs.title: Dive
docs.text:
— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Lets you live and work underwater. Water stops getting in your way:

  • Breathe underwater — never run out of air.
  • Walk the seabed as if it were dry land — no wading, no drag on every step.
  • Mine at full speed — a block underwater breaks as fast as the same block in open air, and the weight a guardian temple puts on your arms lifts while you're under.

Dive takes penalties away; it never hands out a bonus. Push off the bottom and you swim at exactly the speed you always did — if you want to be fast in the water, ride a Pokémon with Surf switched on.

docs.title: Flash
docs.text:
— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Lets you see clearly in the dark, even in caves and at night. Toggle off to remove instantly.

docs.title: Jump
docs.text:
Power: Jump Boost level (default IV)

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Applies continuous Jump Boost. The power value equals the buff level, so power = 4 gives Jump Boost IV. Shows in your HUD.

docs.title: Lava Plume
docs.text:
Power: tenths of the movement multiplier (default 17)

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Dive's twin for lava. It lets you live and work down there: you do not burn, you move through lava and walk its floor without the fluid dragging on every step, and you breathe while you are under. Swimming out is exactly as it always was — like Dive, it takes a penalty away rather than handing out a bonus.

  • Fire: you do not burn while it is on, in lava or out of it.
  • Seeing: with your head under the lava you can see about 24 blocks instead of one, and the floor around you is lit. Wading with your head above the surface leaves the sky as it is.
  • Moving: walking through lava is as quick as walking on land. Sprint and you swim, a little faster, but never faster than you sprint on land.
  • Breathing: your air never runs out while you are under.

Like every aura it only works while its Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks. If it wanders off, goes back in its ball or you switch the aura off, the fire protection lasts 5 more seconds and you get a warning if you are in lava, enough to climb out.

It used to need Burning Bulwark for the fire protection. Burning Bulwark went to Cobblemon Action Combat, so Lava Plume now covers that on its own.

docs.title: Lucky Chant
docs.text:
— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Fortune leans your way while it lasts: what you break and what you fish give up a little more.

docs.title: Magnet Rise
docs.text:
Power: percent of creative flight speed you get (default 25)

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Flight. Switch it on and double-tap jump to lift off, as in creative mode. You stay up for as long as you like, drifting at a little over half your walking pace, and sprinting gives no dash. While it is on you take no fall damage.

It is a building tool, not a way to travel: for that, ride one of your flying Pokémon.

  • It ends when the aura does: recall the Pokémon, switch it off, or get more than 24 blocks from it (flying straight up counts). If that happens in the air, you float down on Slow Falling until you land instead of dropping.
  • Logging out while flying is safe: you come back floating down, and switch it on again once your Pokémon is out.
  • It never touches a flight you have from somewhere else (creative mode, another mod, /fly).

docs.title: Rock Climb
docs.text:
— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Every vertical surface behaves like a ladder, and it is steered by the movement keys: W climbs, S descends, and holding nothing holds your place on the wall.

Your horizontal movement is left alone, so you can travel along a face and step off it whenever you like — a wall is something to climb, not something to be stuck to. On the ground it only takes over when you are actually asking to go up, so walking and jumping near a wall work normally.

It works on your mount too. Riding a Pokémon, run into a wall holding W and your Pokémon climbs it with you.

docs.title: Shadow Sneak
docs.text:
Power: percent of your speed you keep (default 55)

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Total stealth on foot. No footstep sounds, no name over your head, and nothing underfoot notices you — not pressure plates, not tripwires, not a sculk sensor.

You move slower than a walk for it, though faster than a crouch, so it is something you can actually travel in rather than a stationary hiding trick. You cannot sprint on land while it runs, and climbing a ladder or vine makes no sound either.

It only works on land: in water or lava you swim at your normal speed, sprint-swimming included.

If you are already on a scoreboard team

The hidden nametag is done with a vanilla team, so a player who already belongs to one keeps their team and simply does not get that part of the effect. Everything else still applies.

docs.title: Snowscape
docs.text:
Power: trail radius 3

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Winter follows you on foot: snow settles around you as you walk, and still water freezes over as you cross it, the way Frost Walker does. Flowing water is left alone, so a river keeps running instead of being paved, and the ice melts back once you have passed. Where it is too warm to snow (a desert, a jungle, a plain), the snow melts away again shortly behind you; in a cold biome it stays.

  • It works only on foot: not while you ride, swim or fall, so it never freezes the sea under a Pokémon you are surfing on.
  • Only open water freezes. Kelp, seagrass and waterlogged blocks are left as they are, and no ice forms around a creature standing in the water.
  • It changes only what you could change by hand: nothing in adventure mode, in spectator mode or inside spawn protection, and nothing on land a claim mod protects from you.

docs.title: Sweet Scent
docs.text:
Cooldown: 60s between arrivals

Works like a Poké Snack you carry around. While it is on, a wild Pokémon from the area turns up near you about once a minute. It uses Cobblemon's own spawner with the Poké Snack's rules, so what arrives is what lives there, and it never brings a herd.

The held item is the seasoning. Whatever the Pokémon giving off the scent is holding works the way that item would as a Poké Snack seasoning: a berry that leans a snack toward a type, a nature or a shiny leans the scent the same way. Several Pokémon with Sweet Scent on add their items together, like several seasonings in one snack. The item is not used up. A seasoning that makes a snack bite sooner (a bite-time effect) makes the next arrival come sooner too, with the same chance it has in a snack.

Arrivals follow the snack's limits: no more than Cobblemon's Poké Snack cap of wild Pokémon per chunk around you, nothing arrives while you are dead or spectating, and the interval never drops below 5 seconds whatever the config says.

docs.title: Sandstorm
docs.text:
Power: how many times faster loose ground breaks (4)

— how it shows in your status bar while it runs.

Weather aura, with a clear sky. Sand is your ground while it blows:

  • Soul sand and honey never slow you down: you walk on them as fast as on stone. It works in the Nether too, so a soul sand valley is open ground.
  • Sand, gravel, soul sand, soul soil, clay and concrete powder break 4× as fast, whatever you dig them with. Everything else breaks at its normal speed, so it never makes your pickaxe faster.
  • Another player's weather switched on later, close to you, replaces your sandstorm until you move apart or theirs ends.

docs.title: Fog
docs.text:
Power: blocks away a hunter loses you (8)

Weather aura, with a clear sky. A fog rolls in around you and you can only see about 20 blocks. Anything hunting you loses track of you once you are more than 8 blocks away, and goes back to wandering. Up close it still sees you, so Fog is for slipping away, not for standing in the open.

docs.title: Rain Dance
docs.text: Weather aura. It rains, the game's own rain, for as long as Rain Dance is on and its Pokémon is out. Switch it off or recall the Pokémon and Minecraft takes the weather back.

docs.title: Sunny Day
docs.text: Weather aura. The sky stays clear, with no rain and no storms, for as long as Sunny Day is on and its Pokémon is out. Switch it off or recall the Pokémon and Minecraft takes the weather back.

docs.title: Blizzard
docs.text:
Power: radius of the snowfall around you (24)

Weather aura. Snow falls and settles all around you, whatever the biome, for as long as Blizzard is on and its Pokémon is out. The sky stays clear of vanilla rain meanwhile. The snow is real snow: it piles up to three layers and melts on its own, the way any snowfall does in a warm place.
